project: Cosmic Gyoza Express — Tea Moon vertical slice polish

baseline.integratorAssessment: programmer-art tier (~5): fallback serif fonts, debug vectors on by default, flat circles for asteroids, touch pads always visible on desktop, flat rectangles for lunar surface and pad, painted 1280px planets mismatched with pixel ship, no audio.

strengths: Massive improvement over the baseline: every placeholder grey circle and debug overlay is gone, and all art loads with zero fallbacks.
Palette is on-brand: cosmos #17182D base, plum nebula, sage/cream Tea Moon, amber/orange accents that match design-system tokens.
Asteroid cast has real personality (sleepy face, mossy tea rock, mochi, rice). They feel cozy and handcrafted, not hazardous-generic.
Tea Moon destination is a genuine hero moment: the teacup crater, tiny tea house with steam and soft stepped halo read instantly as 'deliver here'.

openIssues: [major] (flight-environment) The nebula parallax 'band' layer does not cover the viewport when the camera scrolls vertically, which exposes a hard horizontal seam (flat cosmos strip) at the top of the screen.

[major] (flight-environment) The hero ship is rendered at a non-integer 0.72 scale of its 144x160 pixel canvas. Nearest-neighbour downsampling drops pixels, so the gyoza body, pleats, legs and glass dome turn into an irregular, blurry strip. It reads lower resolution than the 2x asteroids and moon right next to it, and the hero is the least crisp object on screen.

[major] (flight-environment (FlightHud) + integrator (scale config)) On phoneLandscape the 1280x720 canvas is fit-scaled to about 0.54 (693x390 with pillarbox), so HUD labels, the route note, the destination label and the footer hints render at ~5-6px and blurry. They are unreadable on a phone. The footer also advertises keyboard keys (W/S, A/D, F1) on a phone.

[major] (flight-environment) Background planets are drawn semi-transparent (alpha 0.55-0.6), so star tiles and sparkle stars show through their bodies. They read as ghosts or holograms rather than distant worlds. Planet I'm Fine's bandage reads as a small brown 'X' mark at this opacity.

[minor] (flight-environment) Mixed pixel densities across the flight scene break the 2x pixel contract. Asteroids are scaled to radius*2/bodyArtPx, which is non-integer and differs per rock, and wobble-rotated. Debris uses scale 1 next to scale-2 rocks. Docking and progress rings and the halo are anti-aliased vector circles over crisp pixel art.

[minor] (flight-environment) The approach overlay is cluttered and partly illegible. The dashed ring passes straight through the chevron badge and the 'bottom side' label, the label sits on the light moon surface, and the ghost target-pose silhouette is a muddy dark-grey smudge that doesn't read as the ship.
[minor] (flight-environment) Approach framing crops the Tea Moon landmark: the tea house and chimney are cut off at the right screen edge, so the hero destination isn't fully composed on arrival.

[minor] (flight-environment) Showcase and transition stability. Cruise logs a gyoza-incident bump after the screenshot, so the cruise showcase is on a collision course. The arrival-ready probe/perf window ends in LandingScene with a 66.7ms max frame at the scene hand-off.

[nit] (flight-environment) The off-screen destination label has no backing, so stars sit inside the text and read as stray punctuation ('·25 ·km', '13.km'). The label is also offset left of the pin instead of centred.
[nit] (flight-environment) HUD copy mixes programmer units with fiction units: 'speed 0 px/s' next to 'moon 25.2 km'.

strengths: Huge visual leap over baseline: cohesive dusk palette (plum/navy sky, peach planet, cream ground, terracotta/sage accents) that matches colors_and_type.css warmth
Diegetic landing site: striped blanket on trestles, lanterns that light sequentially on touchdown, cottage with chimney smoke, rabbit NPC who waves on soft landing - strong cozy storytelling
Copy voice is on-brand: lowercase, warm, funny low-stakes failure lines ('moon blanket says: softer, please', 'Emotionally rotated')
Parchment result card with state dot + retry progress bar reads clearly on desktop and matches the UI kit

openIssues: [major] (landing builder (LandingScene / LandingAids)) Thrust flame and the speed gauge are not cleaned up at touchdown. After landing the flame cone keeps drawing in front of the blanket down into the controls pill, the gauge (stale 37/117 value, while the HUD says 0) fades out over the ship and pad, and its soft/bumpy chip slides under the controls bar. This clutters the payoff moment.

[major] (landing builder (LandingTouchPads) + UI kit) Touch landing pads are baseline programmer art (translucent grey circles, plain ^ < > S glyphs, labels overlapping the circle rims), and the steady/thrust pads sit directly over the rabbit NPC and the cottage.

[major] (integrator (Phaser scale/text resolution) + UI kit/landing HUD) Phone landscape text legibility: the 1280x720 canvas is downscaled about 0.54x with nearest sampling, so mono/pixel glyphs lose strokes ('Perfect' renders as 'Pcrfcct', the card subtitle and chatter line are mush). The telemetry panel also takes about 37% x 42% of the game area and crowds the descent airspace.

[minor] (art/ship asset + landing builder) Ship pixel quality: the 144x160 art is displayed at about 0.7x and rotated with nearest sampling, so the dome outline drops pixels and tilted/crashed poses show stair-step smears. Next to the crisp 2x scenery the pixel density is visibly mixed.
[minor] (landing builder / FX shake helper) Incident camera shake moves the HUD panel along with the world and uncovers a 3-4px clear-colour strip along the top and right canvas edges.

[minor] (landing builder (LandingDashboard, landingCopy)) Readout inconsistencies and debug-flavoured units: the HUD descent shows '-24 px/s' while the gauge shows '0', and the 'px' / 'px/s' units read like a dev overlay, not the warm technical dashboard voice.

[nit] (landing builder (LandingPadSite / LandingAids)) Contact shadow and feet: on the settled ship the dark shadow ellipse sits a few px above the blanket's top edge and the legs stop short of the stripe, so the ship reads as hovering. The dashed drop line plus the hard-edged target ring also look slightly vector/debug against the pixel scenery.

[nit] (landing builder / e2e showcase owner) landing:stabilizer was never observed in any capture or playtest probe, so the contract is unverified. Showcase probes are read after the perf window, so the descent and thrust captures log a hard-drop incident that is not what the screenshot shows.

strengths: Huge improvement over the baseline title: a cohesive warm-cosmos palette that matches colors_and_type.css (terracotta, sage, cream parchment, cosmos ink)
Strong typographic hierarchy: Bricolage 800 two-tone title with a warm offset shadow, a clear subtitle, and a distinct Silkscreen CTA
The parchment delivery card reads as handcrafted stationery: dotted divider, corner ticks, portrait, item tile, gentle pill. It balances well against the dominant cosmos.
Saved completion is clearly visible on title-completed: tape sticker, sage 'delivered' pill and a happy portrait swap

openIssues: [major] (ui) Secondary text is unreadable at phone-landscape size. At about 0.54 scale, 11–13 px tokens land at roughly 6–7 px on screen.

[major] (ui (title layout) + art/ship (frames)) The hero ship on the title is weak. It is small (~100 px vs the 140–180 px title size in the design system), rotated 0.16 rad, which breaks the pixel grid and makes the dome jaggy. Its baked flame is a brown heart blob, the thrust puffs look like falling brown rocks, and it floats in dead centre without anchoring the composition.

[major] (ui) Spec gaps on the title: ui-reference asks for secondary actions (settings, credits), but only the CTA and an M-sound keycap exist. On title-completed the CTA is unchanged and there is no route-log entry to view the collected postcard.
[minor] (ui) The left/right touch controls in the ui-kit are thin, low-contrast outline circles with text and no glyph, inconsistent with the filled, iconed thrust tile beside them.

[minor] (ui) The ui-kit button grid is misaligned: route log and settings have different widths, left edges and heights from the primary buttons (wide: launch x=63–315 vs route log x=60–336). Each column also leaves about 170 px of dead space at the bottom.

[minor] (dev-harness + ui) The dev scene launcher shows in every title showcase capture and covers the bottom-left composition (it overlaps the planet on phone). The cropped plum planet at bottom centre also reads as an accidental crop.
[minor] (ui) Phone portrait is disjointed: the moon icon sits far above, the canvas becomes a tiny unreadable strip, and the rotate pill sits far below.
[nit] (ui) The keycaps have no ink or warm border, which the design system asks for. In the gallery, W is drawn pressed with no label, so it looks misaligned.
[nit] (ui) The dashed amber focus ring around the CTA is always on, even for mouse users. It reads like a selection marquee.

[nit] (ui/art) Mixed pixel densities on the title: clouds use about 8 px pixels, the moon about 4 px, the rabbit and teapot about 2–3 px, and the ship is rotated. The 1.5x wide scale gives uneven pixels.

strengths: Audio engine is architecturally excellent: a pure, exhaustive GameEvent mapper (audioCues.ts) separated from Web Audio rendering, all tuning in typed data, and a unit-test file present (tests/audioCues.test.ts).

Gesture-gated AudioContext verified live: 'uncreated' before input, 'running' after a pointer click. Keydown, pointerdown and touchend all unlock. The context suspends and resumes with tab visibility.

Robust mastering chain (glue compressor, then limiter, then tanh soft-clip at -1 dBFS). Offline analysis shows the stacked worst case (result music + thrust + dramatic bump + incident + touchdown + chime) peaking at only -3.6 dBFS, with no clipping and no NaNs.
Graceful failure everywhere: handleEvent, the scheduler, loops and sfx are all try/catch-wrapped, there is a webkit fallback, and nothing runs (silent no-op) until a gesture unlocks the context.

openIssues: [major] (landing (with audio-fx review)) The landing nozzle flame mixes smooth vector rendering into the pixel-art FX. NozzleFlame draws an anti-aliased Graphics triangle plus a banded radial glow disc over the pixel thrust puffs. It is the most prominent FX in the hero landing-thrust state and breaks the pixel cohesion the FX particles otherwise achieve.

[minor] (audio-fx (asset tweak: particles producer)) The dust burst spends visible time in its cool-grey tail frames. Rotated, those split-puff frames read as dark charcoal heart shapes, so the burst looks like soot rather than cozy moon dust or flour. The fx-gallery dust panel shows almost only grey hearts.

[minor] (audio-fx) Mixed pixel density: particles render at about 3 screen px per art px, while the ship sprite (flight about 1 px, landing about 2 px) and the scenery use finer pixel grids. Next to the ship, the trail and dust look chunkier than the world they sit in.

[minor] (audio-fx (event) + ui/hud) There is no in-game feedback for mute. Pressing M silently toggles the master gain, with only a hover tick on unmute. Outside the dev gallery footer, nothing shows the player that sound is off, and the controls hint lists 'M sound' only on title copy.

[minor] (audio-fx) Music mood changes wait for the next bar boundary (8 eighth-steps, about 4.1 s at the 58 bpm flight mood), then the pads take 1.5 s to fade in. Entering a scene can keep the previous scene's mood playing for up to about 5 s, which weakens transitions such as landing to result.

[minor] (audio-fx) The continuous thrust loop (about -23.4 dBFS RMS) is louder than the whole music bed (about -26 dBFS RMS), while soft bump feedback sits around -38 dBFS RMS. Holding W for long flights will mask the lullaby and make soft bumps easy to miss. Rewards (arrival-chime and result-jingle, RMS 0.11 to 0.15) are about 20 dB above bump cues.

[nit] (audio-fx) Transition polish: the flash reads as a neutral grey wash mid-fade rather than warm cream, the iris is a smooth vector circle with a thin anti-aliased stroke, and the warp zooms the camera at non-integer scale, which blurs the pixel UI text during the effect.

[nit] (audio-fx) The dev audio log misreports music. 'music:title' is recorded as not played (x) before the context exists and is never re-recorded once createContext starts the title music, so critics reading lastCues think the title music never played. Also, any exception during createContext permanently sets unsupported=true, even for a transient failure.

strengths: Huge improvement over baseline: production rabbit portrait, item sprites, memory postcard and parchment card replace the serif placeholder text card entirely; zero fallbacks.

Result copy is outstanding and on-brief: 'a spirited delivery', 'That landing sounded like a cupboard. Very comforting, actually.', '2 friendly bumps along the way', 'landed on try 2 · the moon waited' -- warm, never shaming, backed by a banned-words list in src/data/resultCopy.ts.

Clear visual hierarchy: pixel kicker > display headline > quoted reaction > stamps > mono stats > footer actions; the palette (parchment, ink, terracotta, sage/amber pills) matches design-system.md tokens.

Navigation is explicit: labelled 'back to title [esc]' and 'fly again [enter]' buttons with keycaps; pointer taps only skip the staged reveal; event.repeat is ignored; leave() is guarded against double activation.

openIssues: [major] (results builder (DeliveryResultScene)) Stat-row icons are drawn at a non-integer scale (1.5x). This breaks the pixel contract and mixes pixel densities on the card.

[minor] (results builder (with fx/feedback.ts owner if the sparkle config is shared)) Sparkle particles from the postcard reveal are still alive in the settled frame. Over the navy postcard sky they alpha-blend into muddy grey and brown crosses that read as dirt on the art. A stray outlined ✧ also floats over the parchment above the postcard.

[minor] (results builder + art) Pixel art and pixel-font text are rotated by arbitrary angles. The postcard holder is at -2° and the stamp pills are tilted, so their edges and glyphs stair-step against the 2x pixel grid. The postcard tape is flat 55%-alpha amber rectangles, which read as programmer shapes beside the hand-made art.

[minor] (shell/integrator (Phaser scale config) with results builder) Result text is unreadable in phone portrait. The 16:9 canvas is letterboxed to ~350x197, so the card's body text is about 5-7 px. The rotate hint is friendly, but anyone who doesn't rotate can't read the delivery payoff.
[minor] (results builder) Font sizes on the card are off the type scale, which weakens consistency with the official tokens.

[minor] (save/results builder) The future-version and storage-unavailable recoveries are silent. A player on an older build, or with storage blocked, earns progress that disappears on reload, and nothing tells them.
[nit] (results builder / UI kit) The hard shadow under the buttons renders as a separate dark underline with a cream gap. It reads as a detached line rather than a solid 3px pixel lip.

[nit] (save builder / dev tooling) Corrupt-save backup and harness coverage gaps. A second corrupt load overwrites the first backup. The capture probe does not expose the save outcome, so critics can't verify recovery from the JSON alone.

[nit] (dev tooling / results builder) The dev-only 'dev scene launch' panel appears in the title-corrupt-save captures. Composition nit: the backdrop moon's teahouse is clipped at the top edge behind the result card.

strengths: Environment and prop art (asteroids, tea moon, teahouse, pad, lanterns, rocks, rabbit sprite and portrait, items, UI kit) is cohesive, crisp 2px pixel art with ink outlines and a warm palette that matches colors_and_type.css. It is a large improvement over the baseline.
Manifest integrity: all 47 entries exist with exact dimensions and frame strips. 0 failed assets and 0 fallbacks across all states.
Anchors are correct: the ground surface is at row 8 and the pad surface at row 6. The pad, lanterns, rabbit and teahouse sit on the surface line without floating or sinking.
Landing scene composition (dusk gradient, layered hills, warm teahouse, striped pad) reaches the cozy 'Spiritfarer-lite' bar.

openIssues: [major] (ship) The hero ship is the lowest-fidelity asset in the game. It was polished from a blurry, smooth-upscaled source, so it reads as noise next to the crisp asteroids, teahouse and rabbit: broken uneven dome ring, smudged grey shapes inside the dome, scattered stray pixels, and a heart-shaped nozzle floating detached below the hull.

[major] (ship) Mixed pixel density on the ship. The PNGs bake in 2x2 blocks (manifest says artScale 1), and FlightScene draws them at flightScale 0.72, so ship pixels are about 1.44 screen px next to 2 px asteroids. Constant rotation adds shimmer, and the 0.16 rad title tilt resamples it too.

[major] (space) The nebula is double-upscaled. nebula.png is 100% uniform 2x2 blocks (320x180 effective art) but is declared artScale 2, so on screen it renders at 4 px per art pixel. Its chunky stepped cloud edges clash with the 2 px stars, asteroids and moon on the title, flight and result screens.

[major] (planets) Legacy painted planets are loaded but unused, and their style clashes. planet00 and planet04 (1280x1280 smooth painted art, artScale 1) are preloaded through the manifest as planet-tea-moon and planet-im-fine, but nothing in src references them. That costs about 630 KB of download plus about 13 MB of GPU texture for nothing. The other 8 planets (01-03, 05-09) are unreferenced but still ship in public/, about 2.2 MB in the build. Their soft painted rendering does not match the pixel-art direction.

[minor] (items) The teahouse and ship are off-model between assets. The landing teahouse is a round cream cottage with orange shingles. The tea-moon hut and the postcard teahouse are red pagodas on stilts. The postcard ship has a green dome, red dots and an elongated hull, unlike the hero gyoza.
[minor] (particles) The landing thrust flame is a smooth vector triangle drawn by NozzleFlame.ts, not pixel art. It reads as a flat orange cone against the pixel scene.

[minor] (asteroids) The mochi asteroid is softer and noisier than its siblings. A dense checker dither covers the whole body, and the outline is weak or missing on the lit top-right edge, so in flight it reads as a fuzzy pink blob rather than a crisp rock.
[nit] (asteroids) The art-src/_probe/ scratch folder (asteroid-72.png, asteroid-probe.png) has no PROVENANCE.md and looks like leftover experiment output.
[nit] (ui) UI icon 1 ('package') reads as a horned bug face at 16 px. The sound-on icon's waves blur into a dark burst.
